President Trump's campaign push ahead of the midterms
took him to northwest Georgia yesterday,
where he rallied on behalf of Republican Senate nominee
Congressman Mike Collins.
He also repeated false claims about the 2020 elections.
Royal Bali of Member Station WABE has the story.
Trump bounced from topic to topic
during his roughly 90-minute speech
that included several attacks on U.S. Senator John Ossoff,
the only Democratic Senator up for reelection this year
in a state Trump won in 2024.
He does not represent your values,
and he never won the election.
He was in there as an impostor.
Trump referring to the 2020 elections,

The president stopped short of making any claims
on election security related to this year.
For NPR News, I'm Raul Bali in Dalton, Georgia.
Firefighters in Southern California
have been working around the clock
as they try to contain the fast-moving Norte Fire,
which is burning on the border of San Clemente
and San Juan Capistrano.
Orange County Fire Authority Captain Augie Romo
says the high winds opposed a particular challenge.
We knew the increased winds were coming,
and we recognized the elevated fire danger
associated with those conditions.
So because of that, we took the proactive approach
by pre-positioning additional firefighters and equipment
in strategic locations throughout the area.
The fire has exploded to more than 460 acres
and affected at least six homes so far.
Thousands face evacuation orders.
Demonstrators in France are hoping for an alliance
between student protesters and the Yellow Vest movement
that mobilized eight years ago
against high gas prices and the government.
As NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports,
an economic crisis could bring both movements together
in what is being billed as a day of anger.
The French Interior Minister says 90 protest marches
and 500 separate actions are planned across the country.
Social media posts indicate that there could be an alliance
between the students who are protesting dilapidated
facilities, overcrowded classrooms and a lack of teachers,
and a reconstituted Yellow Vest movement
of angry white working-class voters.
Everyone is demanding more government spending
and protections against rising energy prices,
but with France mired in debt
and with record-high borrowing costs,
the government has little room to maneuver.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
President Trump has signed an executive order
that puts on hold sanctions against Russia.
The move comes as Russia continues its war against Ukraine.
The president said the order was a matter
of national interest.
It comes just a week after Trump announced
the U.S. would buy diesel oil from Russia.
You're listening to NPR.
A new report finds the number of people
facing life-threatening hunger
has doubled over the past decade.
NPR's Jonathan Lambert reports food crises
in just three countries account for much of the hunger.
266 million people worldwide are facing acute hunger,
according to a report from the nonprofit Action Against Hunger.
About a third of them live in the Democratic Republic
of Congo, Sudan and Nigeria.
Conflict is a major cause of the crisis.
Ongoing fighting is displacing millions of people
while making it harder to deliver humanitarian aid.
Climate change is playing a role too,
with disasters destroying crops and livelihoods.
And rising poverty in some countries
is putting food out of reach for many.
This increase in hunger is happening as funds to fight it drop.
Humanitarian aid targeting food insecurity
fell by nearly 60% over the past few years.
The authors say that peace and more funding
are needed to reverse the trend.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
Leaf peeping season is upon us.
The Fall Foliage Report website,
which tracks fall foliage,
says this will be an elite year in New England,
thanks to the spring and summer rainfall,
in addition to the warm days and the cool nights
heading into the fall season.
Colorado, on the other hand, is a much different story.
It is having a lackluster foliage season
due to extreme drought conditions.
Fall foliage happens when leaves start making
the green pigment chlorophyll,
and that in turn unmasks those orange and yellow pigments
that were there all along.
I'm Lynda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
